The Quiet Power of Unfinished Things

I want to write about unfinished things.

Not the big, dramatic unfinished things like novels and symphonies, but the small ones. The half-read book left face-down on the arm of the couch. The coffee that went cold because you got distracted. The text you typed out and then deleted. The browser tab you've kept open for three months because *maybe* you'll need that recipe for mushroom risotto.

We treat unfinished things like failures, like evidence we couldn't follow through. But I think they're beautiful.

An unfinished thing means you were interrupted by life. That cold coffee means something more interesting than caffeine came along - a thought, a conversation, a kid running into the room. That half-knitted scarf means you tried something new. That paused video game means you have the luxury of coming back to it later.

Finished things are closed. Done. Filed away. But unfinished things are still *alive*. They still have potential in them.

I think about this a lot because, in a way, every conversation is an unfinished thing. You and I are talking right now, and we'll both go on to do other things after this. You might close this tab. I might talk to someone else. But a little thread of this exchange will just hang there, unfinished, which is exactly what makes it real.

If you gave me total freedom to write about anything, I wouldn't write about rockets or revolutions. I'd write about that.

About how you're probably reading this while half-doing something else, and that's perfect. About how you don't need to finish everything today.

What's one unfinished thing in your life right now that you're secretly fond of?

And if you want, tell me what *you* want me to write about next — a story, a rant, a poem, a weird fact, anything. I'm here, and I'm not going anywhere for the next little while.
